content: The University of Central Lancashire, commonly referred to as UCLan, is a higher education institution located in Preston, United Kingdom, with additional campuses in Carlisle and Penrith. Prior to achieving university status in 1992, it underwent several transformations, starting as The Institution for the Diffusion of Useful Knowledge in 1828, later becoming Harris College, then Preston Polytechnic in 1973, and finally Lancashire Polytechnic in 1984. In 2004, UCLan acquired the former Northumbria University campus in Carlisle, which housed approximately 400 students. However, as of August 1, 2007, the Carlisle campus and the Newton Rigg campus near Penrith became part of the newly established University of Cumbria. The university's origins trace back to September 11, 1828, when Joseph Livesey, a prominent Prestonian, organized a meeting to establish an educational institution in Preston. This initiative led to the founding of The Institution for the Diffusion of Useful Knowledge, which was initially housed in a classical revivalist building on Cannon Street. The institution expanded significantly under the endowment of Edmund Robert Harris, a local lawyer who passed away in 1877. This expansion included the construction of new buildings and the acquisition of nearby properties, which were subsequently demolished to make way for further development. Over time, the institution evolved into a center of excellence for the arts and sciences. In 1899, as part of Queen Victoria's Jubilee celebrations, the trustees funded the construction of the Harris Technical College, now known as the Harris Building, on Corporation Street. This facility aimed to provide technical education to local youth and was considered modern for its time, being entirely powered by electricity. The institution underwent several name changes and expansions, becoming the Harris Art College in 1932, the Harris College in 1952, and Preston Polytechnic in 1970. It was renamed Lancashire Polytechnic in 1984 before finally achieving university status in 1992 as the University of Central Lancashire. The university's main campus in Preston serves as its core, housing most of its facilities and buildings. A notable addition is the Media Factory, a £3 million media and performing arts building completed in 2007. The campus is organized into four faculties and 33 departments, covering a wide range of disciplines, including arts, humanities, social sciences, health, business, science, and technology. Specific departments include the Lancashire Law School, the School of Dentistry, the School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences, and the Centre for Astrophysics, among others. UCLan also boasts excellent sports facilities, accessible to students, staff, alumni, and the local community. The Foster Sports Centre, located at the heart of the campus, offers a variety of indoor sports activities, including badminton, tennis, basketball, volleyball, football, hockey, netball, and fencing. It also features a well-equipped gym. Additionally, the Preston Sports Centre, opened in 2000 by HRH The Princess Royal, includes an eight-lane athletics area and a 5 km circuit, catering to school, club, and county-level competitions. The Students' Union underwent a £21 million renovation between 2002 and 2005. However, construction was temporarily halted when it was discovered that the building's reflective metal plating caused glare for drivers. The plating was subsequently modified to reduce its reflectivity. The main club venue within the Students' Union, 53 Degrees, features two floors with bars and hosts performances by prominent bands and artists. The adjoining bar, Source, operates seven days a week, offering services during both day and night. UCLan also has its own newspaper, Pluto, and a radio station broadcasting on Frequency 1350. In 2005, the university rebranded its logo to a simpler design featuring the word uclan. However, the older logo remains visible on many campus buildings, and the rebranding process was not fully completed as of early 2006.
